summary: Île Greenly light in the Strait of Belle Isle: first lit 13 August 1878, burned 1947, automated 1983; its keeper's house sheltered the 1928 Bremen transatlantic fliers.

lens.note: Department report: second order dioptric single quick-flashing light, 9 July 1906 (LighthouseFriends gives 6 July with a Chance Brothers lens)

structures.note: Quebec register gives 20 m (66 ft); LighthouseFriends gives seventy feet; burned 1947

access.note: Tower closed to visitors (LighthouseFriends). The island is in the Baie de Brador Migratory Bird Sanctuary, whose restrictions apply (Environment and Climate Change Canada). LighthouseFriends says the better view is from the water.

facts.agency: Municipality of Blanc-Sablon (site and buildings, since 1998); Canadian Coast Guard (navigation aid, on its List of Lights)

events.note: Lit 13 August 1878 by first keeper Louis Couillard de Beaumont
Fog gun: thirty-two-pound carronade replaced the nine-pound carronade
Steam foghorn in operation at the opening of navigation
Steam foghorn moved 900 feet to the island's southern end; 900-foot handrail to the light
Heavy open ice filled the Strait from mid-January until about the end of May 1900
Whistle to be replaced by a modern diaphone plant (reported for the year ended 30 June 1905)
New wooden fog-alarm building put in operation 15 August 1906, 695 feet from the lighthouse
Second order dioptric single quick-flashing light put in operation 9 July 1906, replacing a catoptric group revolving light (LighthouseFriends says 6 July)
Tower and keeper's dwelling reshingled and repainted; new oil store
Keeper's dwelling extended; fog alarm building repaired
Baie de Brador Migratory Bird Sanctuary established, covering Île Greenly
Bremen transatlantic fliers came down on a pond near the light; the keeper and family cared for them until they could be rescued
Monument to the Bremen crew dedicated 14 August 1928; cairn built by the keeper and his brother
Steel skeleton tower built to replace the burned light
Station automated; last keeper left; metal tower built
Second light replaced by a skeleton structure carrying an automated light
Site and buildings ceded to the Municipality of Blanc-Sablon

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and the Quebec register both give 1947 for the fire. The Quebec register dates the steel replacement tower to 1949.

LighthouseFriends says both that the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse and that the buildings belong to Blanc-Sablon. The Quebec register says the site and buildings were ceded to the municipality in 1998, which settles the buildings and site.

notes_for_editor: 1) Lens date: the Department's report (cite 9, scan p. 59, printed p. 52) gives 9 July 1906; LighthouseFriends gives 6 July 1906 and a Chance Brothers lens (cite 1). The story gives both. 2) Tower height: Quebec register 20 m (66 ft) (cite 2); LighthouseFriends 'seventy-foot-tall' (about 21 m) (cite 1). The story gives both, metres first. 3) Fire year: 1947 (cites 1, 2). The 1949 steel tower is from the Quebec register. An earlier note cited a 1948 online source; it was not read and is no longer relied on. 4) Keepers 1878-1903 and 1908-1939 come from LighthouseFriends' head-keeper list. The Department's keeper lists confirm only Fagot (1901 list, scan p. 256; the printed page is not confirmed) and Dubois (1904, scan p. 168; 1906, scan p. 176, printed p. 167). The Fagot line is matched by OCR line; the checker should view scan p. 256. 5) The 25 April 1928 Indianapolis Times prints the keeper's name as 'Le Temper' (OCR). The same words are printed by LighthouseFriends under 'Jacques Letemplier, keeper of the lighthouse', and the Washington Times names Letemplier. The checker should view the page image before the spelling is changed. 6) The Washington Times 23 April 1928 byline is legible in the OCR: 'By BARON GUNTHER VON HUENEFELD'. The story now names him from that byline, and the text calls him the Bremen's passenger. An earlier draft said the byline was illegible; that was wrong. 7) The 14 April 1928 Indianapolis Times has a separate 'Snow Falls in Indiana' item (Warsaw, Ind.) whose snowfall sentence was wrongly attached to the Greenly landing. It has been removed from the story and from the evidence. The Montcalm line is from the Greenly item. 8) LighthouseFriends' 1880s-1890s details (Beaumont's salary and allowance, the 1882 carronade, the 1888 foghorn, the 1896 move) are not in the corpus (marine_ca starts with 1900) and rest on LighthouseFriends alone. The 1905 diaphone, the 1906 lens, the 1906 fog building and the 1908 and 1923 work are Department reports, checked by page. 9) The island's ownership: LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse and that the buildings belong to Blanc-Sablon; the Quebec register says the site and buildings were ceded to the municipality in 1998. The story uses the register and does not state a Coast Guard owner. 10) Chesley G. Thomas (1939-1968) and John Thomas (1968-1983) served after about 1960; they are named only as LighthouseFriends lists them as head keepers, with no personal detail. 11) The Bremen replica at Blanc-Sablon airport comes from a LighthouseFriends reader's note; not independently checked. 12) Wikipedia was consulted only for leads and is not cited. The sanctuary page does not mention permits; none are stated in the story. 13) The 1947 fire's cause and any injuries are not in the sources read; the story says so. 14) No wrecks are tied to the station by a source. The Bremen's landing is recorded as a rescue event in the events list (it is a forced landing answered by the keeper and family).
